title: Photoacoustic Spectroscopy Calibration Lab
description: A virtual photoacoustic spectroscopy workstation where the AntiqueCamera serves as a vintage light-source emitter housing (firing tunable photon beams at samples) and the BoomBox acts as an acoustic resonance detector capturing molecular vibration signatures. The user must calibrate wavelength, intensity, and acoustic gain across multiple chemical samples while obeying energy conservation laws, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a photoacoustic spectroscopy calibration lab. Load AntiqueCamera.glb on the left as the 'Photon Emitter' and BoomBox.glb on the right as the 'Acoustic Detector', both on a lab bench (a flat box geometry with dark surface). Place 5 cylindrical sample vials (colored translucent glass materials) on a rotating turntable between them. Camera: perspective at (0,3,6) looking at origin. Lighting: warm directional light plus point lights that change color based on selected wavelength. INTERACTIONS (10-14 steps): 1) Click a vial to load it into the beam path (turntable rotates). 2) A wavelength slider (UV 200nm to IR 1200nm) adjusts the emitter beam color (a visible RaycasterLine from camera model to sample). 3) An intensity dial (0-100%) scales beam brightness and line opacity. 4) An acoustic gain knob (1x-10x) on the BoomBox side scales the detector reading. 5) A 'Fire Beam' button triggers a 1-second animation: beam travels from AntiqueCamera lens to vial, vial glows, acoustic wave rings animate outward toward BoomBox, and a signal value appears on a floating HUD panel. 6) The signal equals (intensity * gain * sampleAbsorptionCoeff[wavelength]) but total energy across all readings is conserved at 1000 units — increasing one sample's allocation reduces the pool for others (shown as an energy bar). 7) User must record readings for all 5 samples by clicking 'Log Reading'. 8) Implement undo/redo buttons that revert any slider change, sample switch, or logged reading using a command stack. 9) Multi-input coupling: changing wavelength auto-adjusts intensity to maintain constant photon flux (they are inversely linked). 10) A completion check button validates all 5 samples are logged with signal above threshold. Use dat.gui or HTML overlay controls. Show energy conservation bar prominently. Add OrbitControls for scene inspection.
